hookups.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/233284 (notice: 'There are no showers or electric, water or sewer hook-ups in the park.') + https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/cataloochee-campground.htm ('No hookups or showers are available in the campground'; 'Electric Hookups: 0'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: NPS: RV and trailer max 31 ft. The recreation.gov catalog lists 27 standard non-electric sites with max vehicle lengths of 20 to 34 ft (nine at 32 ft), all back-in but one pull-through. Access road advisory: 'Motorhomes over 29' and trailers over 25' in length are not recommended due to the access road' (a 3-mile gravel stretch of Cove Creek Road with narrow, blind curves and steep drop-offs without guard rails).

sites.source: https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/cataloochee-campground.htm ('TOTAL SITES: 27'; 'RV Max Length in Feet - 31'; 'Trailer Max Length in Feet - 31') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/233284 (notice quoted) + RIDB catalog 233284 (Max Vehicle Length, Driveway Entry), read 2026-10-22

values.note: Flush toilets and drinking water are seasonal; no cell reception or internet. Nearest RV dump stations are at other park campgrounds (Cades Cove, Cosby, Deep Creek, Look Rock, Smokemont).

facilities.source: https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/cataloochee-campground.htm (Amenities: 'Cell Phone Reception No; Internet Connectivity No; Camp Store No; Laundry No; Dump Station No; Potable Water - Seasonal'; 'Toilet Types Flush Toilets - seasonal'; 'Shower Types None') + https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/frontcountry-camping.htm (dump stations), read 2026-10-22

values.note: NPS: 'Cataloochee Campground closes seasonally ... Closed October 25–May 1'; recreation.gov sold nights through October 25, 2026.

season.source: https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/cataloochee-campground.htm (Operating Hours & Seasons: 'Closures & Seasonal Exceptions Closed October 25–May 1'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: Reservations required and site-specific; book before driving in, as there is no cell coverage and no way to reserve at the campground. Park-wide limit 14 consecutive nights and 60 nights a year.

booking.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/233284 ('A reservation is required to stay at Cataloochee Campground ... there are no provisions to make a reservation once you are at the campground'; 'The park stay limit is 14 consecutive days') + https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/cataloochee-campground.htm ('Campsite reservations are required and may be made up to six months in advance.'), read 2026-10-22

fees.source: https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/cataloochee-campground.htm ('Camping Fee is per site, per night. Reservations are required. $30.00') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/233284/rates (2026 Peak Season May 1 - Oct 25, standard non-electric $30), read 2026-10-22

discounts.source: https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/frontcountry-camping.htm ('If you are 62 or older or have a permanent disability, you may be eligible for the senior or access pass ... These two passes do provide discounts on camping fees.'), read 2026-10-22

note: Great Smoky Mountains National Park; in a high valley surrounded by even higher mountain peaks.  --AWH
summary: NPS page (read in a browser) + recreation.gov: confirmed 27 sites, $30/night, no hookups. Added NPS max 31 ft (catalog 20-34 ft, one pull-through) with the road advisory, season May 1 - Oct 25 (status open now), reservations required on recreation.gov up to six months ahead (fcfs never), 14-night limit, flush toilets and drinking water (seasonal), no showers/dump/laundry/store/internet, senior/access camping discount. Note: dropped AWH's '27 sites for tents and RVs.' (now in sites.count).
flags: Access road advisory (recorded, not a criteria failure for a 23-ft rig): 'Access to Cataloochee is via a narrow, winding, mountain road. A 3-mile stretch of gravel road contains many narrow, blind curves. Motorhomes over 29' and trailers over 25' in length are not recommended due to the access road.' NPS adds steep drop-offs with no guard rails and that drivers may need to back up to pass. No 4WD or high-clearance advisory.
Missing phone: the entry has none. NPS lists the campground at 828-269-3161 (recreation.gov gives 828-497-9270). Operated by NPS directly (not commercially managed).
